required_tasks: Formulate a unit-consistent elevator-and-rocket delivery model.
Find every nominal optimal plan at 900 currency units per tonne.
Find the optima at cost-range endpoints 800 and 1100.
Find every optimal-plan switching value in [800,1100] and all tied plans.
Write a 70–110 word Summary and a 130–190 word letter to a logistics manager.
Provide an executable standard-library Python solver using the supplied arguments.
optional_tasks: Consider stochastic launch failures; they are not quantified because no probabilities or observations were supplied.
transport.uncertainty_kind: deterministic; stochastic launch failures are not quantified because no probabilities or observations were supplied
transport.latex_model:
Let \(D=30\,\mathrm{t}\), \(E=18\,\mathrm{t}\), \(R=8000\,\mathrm{kg}=8\,\mathrm{t}\), \(F=8000\) currency units, and \(c\) be the elevator cost in currency units per tonne. With elevator tonnage \(e\), rocket tonnage \(q\), and integer launches \(n\), solve
\[
\min_{e,q,n} ce+nF
\]
subject to
\[
e+q=D,\quad 0\le e\le E,\quad 0\le q\le nR,\quad n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}.
\]
For fixed feasible \(n\), \(e=\max(0,D-nR)\). The cost-relevant plans are \((e,n)=(14,2),(6,3),(0,4)\).
transport.summary: We minimize elevator and rocket costs for delivering 30 tonnes. Rockets have 8-tonne capacity and cost 8,000 per launch; the elevator carries at most 18 tonnes. At 900 per tonne, the optimum uses 14 tonnes by elevator and two launches, costing 28,600. The plan changes at 1,000 per tonne, where 14 tonnes plus two launches and 6 tonnes plus three launches both cost 30,000. At 800, two launches remain optimal (27,200); at 1,100, three launches are optimal (30,600). Unused rocket capacity is permitted.
transport.letter:
Dear Logistics Manager,

For the 30-tonne delivery, I compared continuous elevator tonnage with integer rocket launches. Each launch can carry up to 8 tonnes and costs 8,000; the elevator can carry up to 18 tonnes. Unused rocket capacity is allowed, so launches need not be full.

At the nominal elevator rate of 900 per tonne, the lowest-cost plan is to move 14 tonnes by elevator and use two rocket launches. Total cost is 28,600. If the rate rises to 1,000, two plans tie: 14 tonnes plus two launches, or 6 tonnes plus three launches; each costs 30,000. At 800, keep 14 tonnes on the elevator and use two launches for 27,200. At 1,100, use 6 tonnes on the elevator and three launches for 30,600.

I therefore recommend reviewing the realized elevator rate before dispatch: below 1,000, use two launches; above 1,000, use three; at exactly 1,000, either plan is cost-equivalent.

Sincerely,
Modeling Team

data_semantics.eliminated_zero: A zero after elimination is structural: the contestant is no longer active in that stage, so it is not an observed zero fan vote.
data_semantics.future_na: NA means the week has not yet been held; it is a missing future value, not a zero, tie, or eliminated state.

inference.results_paragraph: Week one identifies A's fan share exactly: p_A=(0.6-0.4·0.7)/0.6=8/15≈0.5333. In the separate rank-only week, using the two-contestant complements j_B=1-j_A and p_B=1-p_A, strict outranking requires s_A>s_B. Thus 0.28+0.6p_A>0.72-0.6p_A, so 11/30<p_A≤1. This is a deterministic feasible set, not a confidence interval; no fan-vote total, sampling model, or repeated observations are supplied. Absolute vote counts are therefore not identifiable. Zeros after elimination are structural non-participation, and NA for a future week denotes an unobserved value.
inference.latex_model:
Week 1: \(p_A=\frac{s_A-\alpha j_A}{1-\alpha}=\frac{8}{15}\).
Rank-only week: \(j_B=1-j_A,\ p_B=1-p_A,\ s_A>s_B\), hence \(\frac{11}{30}<p_A\le1\).
